This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Sri.Gangadhara.G. caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
On 21.09.2024, at about 5.20 a.m., Gangadhara G. was standing by the roadside near Anchepalya Skywalk on the Tumakuru-Bengaluru NH-48 Highway at Bengaluru and was giving signals to other vehicles.

At that time, an Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643, came from Tumakur towards Bengaluru was drove the same in a rash and negligent manner by it driver and dashed against the Gangadhara G,
Obanna and 407 Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA- 16-A-4211.
Due to said the impact,Gangadhara G. has sustained grievous injuries all over the body and died while being shifted to the hospital.
Postmortem was conducted at Government hospital, Nelamangala and the petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards death and obsequies ceremony of deceased.

Nethramma vs Amjad Basha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139742107/
2 3.

Prior to the accident, deceased Gangadhara.G was hale and healthy, he was aged about 45 years at the time of his death, by doing agriculture he was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month and contributed his entire earning to the maintenance of the family and the petitioners are depending entirely on the income of the deceased.

Due to death of deceased, the 1st petitioner, who is the wife,
has lost her loving husband and marital life, 2nd, 3rd and 4th petitioners are children have lost their loving father and 5 th petitioner, who is the mother of deceased has lost her loving son.
Hence, all the petitioners are suffering from mental shock and income of their family has been deprived.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of above said Eicher Canter in Cr.No.390/2024.
Accordingly, the petitioners have prayed to award compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- from the respondents.
4. After service of summons, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before this Tribunal and filed separate written statement.
5. Respondent No. 1 has, in his written statement, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.

This respondent has denied the date, time and place of accident, cause of accident due to rash and negligent driving of Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-6343 by its driver, injuries sustained by the deceased and his death due to accident, amount spent by the petitioners towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of deceased.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
This Respondent has contended that Crime No.390/2024 was registered against the driver of the vehicle without conducting a proper investigation.
It is further submitted that the FIR was registered in a mechanical manner and that the driver has been falsely implicated to claim compensation.
Further contended that, the offending vehicle has been insured with the 2nd respondent and it was valid as on the date of accident.
If any compensation is awarded, the 2nd respondent has to pay the same.
Hence, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. The Respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy with respect to Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643 and contended that, the liability to indemnify the owner is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, provision of MV Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of Car at the time of accident.

It is further submitted that the petition is bad for non-joinder of a necessary party, as the driver of the offending vehicle has not been arrayed as a party to the proceedings, hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that, the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle has not complied Sec.134(c) of M.V.Act.
It has denied age, avocation and income of the deceased, rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver and also denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
This Respondent seeks permission under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It is further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving his vehicle in a cautious and careful manner.
However, the deceased was standing in the center of the said road, having parked his tempo without giving any signal, in a negligent manner and failed to observe traffic rules.
Therefore, the deceased alone is responsible for the alleged accident.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues has been framed :
ISSUES Nethramma vs Amjad Basha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139742107/

1. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Ganggadhara.G. S/o. Gangappa?

2. Whether the petitioner's proves that, on 21.09.2024 at about 05.20 a.m., the deceased was standing at the road side and giving signals to other vehicles near Anchepalya skywalk, Tumakuru-Bengaluru NH- 48 highway road, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of the Eicher canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643 drove in a high speed and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
As a result, accident occurred and deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body and he succumbed while shifting to the hospital as mentioned in claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent?
4. What Order or Award?
8.
In order to prove their case, the 1st petitioner herself examined as PW.1 and got marked 25 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 25.
The respondents have not adduced their rebuttal evidence and respondents' evidence is taken as nil.
9. Heard the arguments from broth side.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

Therefore,
petitioners No.1 to 5 are considered as dependents on the income of deceased and they are considered as legal heirs of deceased.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

12. ISSUE No.2:- It is the case of the petitioners that, On 21.09.2024, at about 5.20 a.m.,
Gangadhara G. was standing by the roadside near Anchepalya Skywalk on the Tumakuru-Bengaluru NH-48 Highway in Bengaluru and was giving signals to other vehicles.

At that time, an Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643, came from Tumakuru towards Bengaluru and drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the deceased Gangadhara G.
Due to said the impact, he fell to the side of the road, sustained grievous injuries and died while being shifted to the hospital.
In support of their contention, the 1st petitioner examined herself as P.W.1.
P.W.1 has filed affidavit by way of examination-in-chief and reiterated the petition averments.

To prove the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643, P.W.1 has produced documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.25.
13.
On the other hand, the 1st respondent contends that the driver of the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the accident for the purpose of claiming compensation.

The specific contention of the 2 nd respondent is that the deceased was standing in the center of the road, having parked his tempo without giving any signal, acted negligently and failed to observe traffic rules, therefore, the deceased alone is responsible for the alleged accident.
In support of their contentions, the driver of Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643 has not been examined by the respondents.
The respondents have neither examined any witness and nor produced any documents to believe their contention.
Hence, the contention of respondents holds no water.

14. From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint from one Mahantesh as per Ex.P.2, Nelamangala police have registered the case as per Ex.P.1 i.e., FIR in Crime No.390/2024 against the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643 for the offenses punishable U/s.281, 125 (a), 106 of BNS.
The police have conducted the panchanama on the spot of accident as per Ex.P.3 and prepared the hand sketch map as per Ex.P.5 and inquest panchanama as per Ex.P.6.
The police have seized the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.4.

Ex.P.7 is the postmortem report of the deceased and as per this documents, the death is due to cardiac arrest and shock hemorrhage resulting from injuries sustained in the head and upper spinal region and other injuries sustained in RTA.
Ex.P.10 is the IMV report which shows that, the accident was not occurred due to mechanical defect.

After due investigation the police have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D- 3643 for the offenses punishable U/s.281, 125(a), 125(b), 106 of BNS as per Ex.P14.
Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined of PW.1 in detail, but he has failed to elicit anything to disbelieve his version.
The respondents have not adduced the rebuttal evidence and not produced any documents to disprove the case of the petitioners.

15. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused Nethramma vs Amjad Basha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139742107/
5 by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same"
16.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge- sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by her.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643 for the cause of accident is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.3:

As already discussed in Issue No.1 and 2, Petitioner No.1 to 5 are the dependents of the deceased Gangadhara.G and they are entitled for compensation.
18. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:-
According to petitioners, the deceased Gangadhara G was aged about 45 years at the time of his death.
PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of deceased at Ex.P.17 and it shows that, the date of birth of deceased Gangadhara G is 01-01-1978.
The accident was occurred on 21-09-2024.
Therefore,as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 46 years 8 months 20 days.
Hence the deceased age is considered as 46 Years for purose of multiplier.

As per the principles laid down by their Lordships in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation), the multiplier applicable to the present case is '13'.
19.

20. As the deceased was 47 years as on the date of accident and same is considered as age of the deceased and proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 13.
As the age of the deceased is below 50 years, 25% future prospects have to be added as per Pranay Sethi case.

Then the monthly Nethramma vs Amjad Basha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139742107/

Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, deceased was married and four persons are dependents, hence 1/4 of the income to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and then the annual income would comes around (20,625/- (-) 5,156/-) .15,469/- x 12 = .1,85,628/- and by applying 13 multiplier, the loss of dependency would be .24,13,164/-.

towards Funeral expenses.

24. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

7 25.
In this case, respondent No.1 is the RC owner of offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643 and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer.
The respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its validity at the time of accident with respect to above said vehicle.
Hence, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to the compensation to the Petitioners.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-35-D-3643 is liable to pay compensation Rs.26,89,164/- with 6% interest to the petitioners from the date of petition till deposit the amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative'.

26. ISSUE No.4 :- In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
:: ORDER ::
The petition filed U/sec.166 of M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,89,164/- (Rupees Twenty Six Lakhs Eighty Nine Thousand One Hundred and Sixty Four only) with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.2  insurance company is hereby directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 45%
 Petitioner No.2 to 4 - 15% each  Petitioner No.4 - 10%
Out of the total compensation  amount, entire apportionment  amount shall be disbursed to  petitioner No.1 to 2 and petitioner  No.5 through E-payment on proper  identification.
